ac2a98632cbd32cd.brief: The question asks whether the first published FRED DGS10 value for 2026-11-27 will be strictly above 4.92 percent (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10). No official page could be opened, so every level comes from search snippets. FRED snippets show 5.12 for 2026-11-16 and 5.10 for 2026-11-17, a fourth straight session above 5.00. A Dow Jones item dated 2026-11-19 reports the 10-year at 5.051%, down 0.014 point, the lowest since Nov 10 and four straight declines (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202611198503/10-year-treasury-yield-falls-to-5051-data-talk). Earlier in the month the series was 4.90 on 2026-11-04, 4.84 on 2026-11-05 and 4.86 on 2026-11-06, and the Treasury par yield was 4.98% on 2026-11-10, so 4.92 sits inside the month's range. No value for 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-24 was found. The observation date is the Friday after Thanksgiving; SIFMA recommended a full bond-market close on 2026-11-26 and a 2:00 p.m. ET early close on 2026-11-27 (snippet only). That leaves about six sessions from the last known level, and the 13 bp gap is roughly one standard deviation of a typical 5-6 session move in yields, which gives a base rate for staying above the line of somewhat better than half but not overwhelming. No scheduled rate-moving release, auction or Fed event falls before the observation; the December FOMC (Dec 8-9), November CPI (Dec 10) and the jobs report (Dec 4 or 8) are all later. The shortened session can add noise to the final level. Earlier thresholds set near the then-current level resolved mixed (above 4.86 on Nov 13: yes; above 4.94 on Nov 6: no; above 5.00 on Oct 30: no; above 5.10 on Oct 23: no). The answer would change if a verified FRED or Treasury print for Nov 20-24 showed the 10-year already near or below 4.92, or well above 5.05, or if a data surprise or a Fed repricing hit on Nov 25.
